scope: Proposition 7.4 (Diagonal reset) of the manuscript “Absolutely Continuous Spectrum for Weak-Disorder Anderson Models in Dimensions at Least Three” (preprints/Absolutely-Continuous-Spectrum-for-Weak-Disorder-Anderson-Models-in-Dimensions-at-Least-Three-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 261 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 0d971c56f6ba1641), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 75. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let g = (M − t diag r)−1 on a nonempty active set, where M is real symmetric, r is bounded, and 0 < c ≤ pi = ℑri ≤ C. Assume ker D = C1. Suppose qi = ℑgii ≤ C, the lag e′ = diag(g)−r satisfies ∥e′∥∞ = o(t.36δ) uniformly in the construction parameters, and ∥K∥ < 1 2, ∥(I − K)−1 ∥∞→∞ ≤ C log(1/t). For small t there is a measurable vector ζ, with ∥ζ∥∞ ≤ t.35δ, such that for r′ = r + ζ and g′ = (M − t diag r′)−1 one has g′ ii = r′ i. Writing ρ = ∥ζ∥∞, the changes satisfy max i ∥∆hi∥2 ≤ Cρ, max i,j |∆hij| ≤ C √ t ρ, max i ∥∆hi∥4 ≤ Ct1/4 ρ, (150) ∥K′ − K∥ ≤ Cρ, (1 − Cρ)D ≤ D′ ≤ (1 + Cρ)D. (151) Here D′ uses p′ = ℑr′, which remains in a fixed positive bounded range. The corresponding inverse forms on neutral charges change by a factor 1 + O(ρ).
